chunks: And from him, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram getting cupped (hijamah). He said, 'I do not like it.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.لَا أُحِبُّهُ: I do not like it (indicating recommended avoidance or mild dispreference in fiqh)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in ihram to get cupped?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses a preference against cupping (*hijamah*) for one in *ihram*, reflecting the scholarly consensus that while not strictly forbidden, it is disliked due to the potential for weakness or bleeding which might hinder the pilgrim's rituals. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving the physical state of the pilgrim during the sacred rites, aligning with the broader principle of avoiding acts that may cause unnecessary hardship or distraction from worship.
